title: Introduce regional load-shedding + circuit-breaker integration (hotfix for overload incidents)
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Emergency hotfix that introduces a region-aware load-shedding policy, integrates a per-backend circuit breaker, and wires SLO enforcement hooks into the router. Motivation: Over the last two incidents (SUP-1123) we observed global ingress spikes causing tail-latency SLO violations and cascading overload across regions. This change enables graceful degradation by shedding non-critical requests, tripping regional circuit breakers before node-level queues grow unbounded, and providing operator-visible SLO metrics to drive automatic fallback to cheaper/compatible model variants.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a new load_shed module that makes shedding decisions based on request priority, current regional token SLO headroom (30s rolling), and available KV-cache hit rate. Introduces a circuit_breaker facade that tracks recent error rate and latency percentiles per backend pool and exposes an OpenMetrics endpoint for circuit state. Adds configuration knobs to helm values for region-level thresholds and a feature flag (feature.flag.load_shedding) for staged rollout. Updates the routing policy to consult both the circuit breaker and load-shed decision before enqueueing a request; when shedding occurs we return structured error responses (422 with x-redwood-shed-reason header) to enable client fallbacks. Adds e2e and unit tests for the policy and a small canary rollout plan in the README.

Design notes: - SLO enforcement: we consume the existing slo-proxy metrics (slo_window: 30s) and compute available headroom = max(0, slo_target - recent_error_budget_consumption). The load_shed decision uses headroom and expected token load (estimated by prompt length histogram) to decide whether to accept, queue (if under queue-cap), or shed. - Circuit breaker: hybrid sliding-window + exponential backoff. States: CLOSED -> HALF_OPEN -> OPEN. Open transitions when error_rate > configured_threshold or p95 latency > latency_threshold for the window. Half-open probes are limited by probe_rate config. - Regional failover: when a regional circuit opens, routing attempts cross-region failover to the next prioritized region list (configurable), using model-compatibility map; if no compatible region available, we fall back to lower-cost model variant. - Observability: emits metrics redwood_load_shed{region,reason}, redwood_circuit_state{region,backend,state}, and slo_headroom_bytes. Adds an alert rule to fire when regional shed rate > 5% sustained for 5m.

Files changed (high level): src/runtime/load_shed.py, src/runtime/circuit_breaker.py, src/router/route_decision.go, infra/helm/values-regional.yaml, docs/ops/region-failover.md, tests/e2e/test_load_shed.py, observability/alerts/slo_rules.yaml, scripts/hotfix_apply.sh

Checklist (completed): - [x] Implement load-shedding heuristics and circuit breaker core - [x] Add feature flag and helm values for regions - [x] Unit tests for decision logic - [x] E2E test that simulates regional overload and verifies fallback - [x] Observability: metrics and alert rule - [x] Short canary rollout docs and rollback steps

Testing and CI: Initial CI run failed due to a flaky e2e that depended on timing of p95 samples; test rewritten to use deterministic time window and CI rerun passed. Performance microbenchmarks show <2% p99 regression for accepted requests and a 3x reduction in queue growth during overload scenarios in the staging cluster.

Rollout plan: Feature-flagged. 1) Enable in staging for region us-east (canary) with shed_rate target 1% for 2h. 2) Expand to us-west and eu for 6h with probes enabled. 3) If no regressions and alerts quiet, increase thresholds and enable globally. Rollback: flip feature flag off and promote previous bundle via hotfix_apply.sh (included).

Operational notes: The shed reasons are: low_headroom, circuit_open, queue_full. Clients should implement retry/backoff using x-redwood-shed-reason. We added runbook excerpt to docs/ops/region-failover.md.

Related: Linear ENG-2042 (SLO-driven load-shedding), SUP-1123 (customer outage post-migration).

TODOs for follow-ups: - Integrate with Optimize to recommend per-workload thresholds - Add per-customer SLA-aware shedding in Dedicated mode - Add automatic model-variant fallback scoring

review_comments: Marco Hu (2026-02-21): Overall looks good. Two requests: 1) add a unit test to validate that low_headroom + large prompt triggers immediate shed; 2) ensure prometheus metric names follow our naming convention (use redwood_load_shed_total).
Aisha Patel (2026-02-21): Added the explicit unit test and renamed metrics to follow convention. PTAL.
Lena Ortiz (2026-02-22): We should be conservative with default thresholds; recommend 1% shed_rate default. Also flag the alert as P2 by default.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-22): Set defaults to conservative values (1% initial) and marked alert severity P2 in the rule body.
Samuel Green (2026-02-23): Found a race when circuit transitions to HALF_OPEN under heavy probe load; suggested limiting concurrent probes to 1 per backend.
review_responses: Aisha Patel (2026-02-23): Reduced probe concurrency to 1 and added a stress test to verify transition stability.
Marco Hu (2026-02-24): LGTM after tests. Approving for merge.
Lena Ortiz (2026-02-24): Approve — please bump changelog entry in next patch release.
release_notes: Hotfix: Added regional load-shedding and circuit breaker integration to improve reliability under cross-region overloads. Feature-flagged; conservative defaults. Emits new metrics for monitoring. See docs/ops/region-failover.md for runbook.
notes_for_release_manager: This is a hotfix merged via squash. Enable feature.flag.load_shedding=false by default in production control plane; follow rollout plan in PR description to flip to true in staging then progressively increase scope.
small_snippets:
# samples: helm values (infra/helm/values-regional.yaml)
regionOverrides:
  us-east:
    loadShed:
      enabled: true
      headroom_threshold: 0.01
      queue_capacity: 128

# router decision pseudocode (src/router/route_decision.go)
if circuit.IsOpen(backend) { attemptRegionalFailover() } else if loadShed.ShouldShed(request) { respondShed() } else { enqueue(request) }
